newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 9.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 9.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
** Sonia Gandhi's entry into formal Indian politics breathes life into a dispirited Congress party that longs for the heady days of the Gandhi-Nehru dynasty.
But her role within the nation's oldest party may well remain modest, for the Italian-born widow could be an easy target for critics if she sought a public position of power, analysts said.
Sonia Gandhi decided to join Congress after refusing membership for years, members of parliament said on Thursday.

** Foreign investors have adopted a wait-and-see attitude due to political uncertainties in India but the overall trend is positive and encouraging, a senior official of HSBC Investment Bank Plc said on Thursday.

"I think there is a desire to invest and they are just taking a wait-and-see attitude before committing themselves," Paul Selway-Swift, chairman of HSBC Investment Bank Asia Holdings Ltd, told Reuters.

** Standard & Poor's, a leading global rating service, has signed a share purchase agreement to acquire a 9.6 percent stake in Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd, a company statement said on Friday.
"These shares are currently held by the Asian Development Bank, which invested in CRISIL in 1988 to play a catalytic role in its establishment," the statement said.
** Blue-chip shares at India's National Stock Exchange (NSE) firmed on Thursday helped by tax breaks and hopes of economic revival, brokers said.
** The NSE's 50-stock index rose 9.65 points, or 0.92 percent, to close at 1,054.05. The Bombay Stock Exchange was closed for a local holiday on Thursday.
** Banking and software shares are seen rising after staging a blistering rally at the NSE on Thursday buoyed by hopes of economic revival and helped by tax breaks, dealers said.
** Shares of Sundram Fasteners ended a shade lower at 613.0 rupees after the company posted a small rise in 1996/97 (April-March) net profits.
** Hindustan Motor shares closed little changed at 15.40 rupees after the firm announced a 23 percent fall in 1996/97 net profits.
** Shares of CRISIL will be in the spotlight on news that Standard & Poor's had signed a share purchase agreement to acquire a 9.6 percent stake in the firm.
CRISIL shares ended marginally higher at 274.35 rupees at the National Stock Exchange on Thursday.
